correctness.rationale: The proof establishes a bijection between ideals and triples (W,D,f) with commutator contained in D, including all nongraded lifts. The tensor commutator rank is exactly rb+as-rs. Vector-space Goursat counts all fixed-projection subspaces by quotient dimension h, and Gaussian coefficients count D; multiplying counts and dimensions gives the universal formula. Embedded verify.py separately checks all RREF subspaces for six small cases; tests are corroborative only.

originality.rationale: The finite-field ideal dimension polynomial is not stated in inspected primary material. Closest and strongly overlapping arXiv:1903.03090 identifies exactly this abstract family and computes its p-adic ideal zeta function, but the latter aggregates by index and does not distinguish finite-field elementary-quotient ideal ranks; Section 4 does supply closely related projection-counting machinery, a serious priority/derivability risk. arXiv:2308.00272 treats selected graph-ideals and graded derivations. Claims of uniqueness are avoided.
residual_risks: The 2019 p-adic ideal-zeta paper studies the identical family; although its stated univariate zeta does not imply the finite-field dimension distribution, its projection-counting proof could yield this specialization with limited additional work.
An equivalent finite-field rank enumerator might appear in older Lie ideal-lattice or group normal-subgroup literature not recovered by query searches.

value.rationale: All ideals in every dimension of a natural graph-based two-parameter class-two Lie family over every finite field are enumerated with one positive Gaussian sum. It refines graph-selected ideals and aggregated p-adic index counts by an exact finite-field object invariant, includes nongraded lifts and characteristic two, and supports direct structural counts. It is a full family result rather than a narrow arbitrary parameter slice or a simple low-order record.
